title: Book One · Chapter 105: The Hole Through the Pages
story:
Miss Wu makes holes through the class book.

The children watch from the other side of the desk. Miss Wu uses a sharp tool to make the holes. She puts a thick board underneath the pages. She checks the pages. They are straight. Then she presses down.

Ronan hears a soft crunch. The first hole goes through every page.

“That is the hardest part,” Leo says.

“For the tool,” Miss Wu replies. “You did quite a lot already.”

She gives them thick thread and a large blunt needle. The thread will hold the pages together. They will pass it through the ready holes while she watches. They will not make new holes themselves.

Mei checks the page order once more. The clay shapes come first. Then paper boats, wood tests and the river pictures. The last two pages have their results. They also list more tests for later.

One page is upside down.

Ronan sees it before they put thread through it. It belongs to another group. He shows the group their upside-down picture. He does not laugh at their names below it.

The group turns it. Everyone waits another minute.

When Ronan's turn comes, he pulls the thread too hard. The pages bend into a shallow curve. Miss Wu asks him to loosen the thread. The book needs to open flat.

“Your book looks like a boat,” Leo says.

Ronan smiles and loosens the thread a little. There is room for the pages to turn now.

Each group gets to sign the inside cover. Ronan writes his name. Mei writes hers with a little space beside it. Leo signs after his two partners, not above them.

The cover has three blue waves and a title. Ronan runs a finger beside the dry paint. Before, he wanted a whole blue sea. The small waves look clear against the white paper.

“Where shall we keep the book?” Miss Wu asks. Some children want it in the cupboard. It will stay safe there. Others choose the low shelf. They can reach the low shelf. They can read the book there.

They choose the low shelf. A cloth cover will keep dust off. Miss Wu says they may turn the pages. Their hands must be clean and dry. The pages will not stay new with all that reading. Miss Wu does not mind that.

At break, Ronan watches two children turn the pages. One stops at the picture with Leo's finger. He laughs at the finger above the stones.

Leo is standing nearby. He looks at the page. “My helpful finger was too helpful.”

The children read the words below it. Then they turn to the next page. They do not call Leo names.

“Do you want to take your loose pictures home?” Mei asks Ronan. The class book uses their clean copies, not every early page. He gathers the sheet with the clay marks. He takes the first torn-corner drawing too.

He has more paper now, not less. He wants to keep the best result. He could throw the messy pieces away.

Mei agrees to keep three of their early pages. Ronan puts these in their shared folder. The rest can be used as scrap.

At home, he shows Mum the three. “Which picture do you like most?” she asks. He points to the leaning paper boat. It is crooked, grey and much too large. He remembers their next step. He points to the old picture. Now he can explain it easily to Mum.
studyGuide:
## 重点表达

- thread＝装订用的线
- blunt＝钝的
- loosens＝松开一点
- turn the pages＝翻页

额外情节词（不要求本章全部记住）：needle＝针；thread＝线；curve＝弯曲形状。

## 读句提示

**Where shall we keep the book?**

我们／将把书放在／哪里？完整直接问句。

## 理解问题

1. 大家怎样安全地装订项目书？
2. Ronan为什么留下几张不漂亮的旧记录？
